Area.evidence_source: They were strong-willed with regard to making their own decisions, but (as was said about 14 of them) they frequently also had a strong desire to control others. The relatives experienced that the elderly people set the terms and "took all the decisions". In a family context, and particularly where children were concerned, this was viewed as causing conflicts. The elderly were perceived as strong, and some of them could not stand being contradicted. According to one son, his father's fixed expression was "Either you're with me or you're against me."; Others expressed respect for the strength of the elderly, as one daughter who said: "Yes, he didn't only control those around him but also himself. Mostly himself, I would think."
